title: AnimationMixer applies Node3D scale animation tracks in parent space when combining position/rotation/scale
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: Godot 4.7-stable (4.7 branch, commit 1a5d818ea97) - Not reproducible in: Godot 4.6.3-stable ### System information Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS - Godot v4.7.0 (custom build, 4.7 branch, commit 1a5d818ea97) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (nvidia, driver version unknown) - 13th Gen Intel Core i5-13600KF (16 Threads) ### Issue description When an Animation has `position_3d`, `rotation_3d`, and `scale_3d` tracks targeting the same Node3D node (standard glTF TRS import), Godot 4.7 applies the transform differently than 4.6.3, causing incorrect visual results. Symptoms: - The Inspector `Scale` value for the animated node no longer matches the original keyframe values. - Child nodes (MeshInstance3D, GPUParticles3D) are visibly distorted due to unexpected basis composition. - Particle AABBs are deformed by the parent node's incorrect transform. The root cause is in commit `1a5d818ea9` ("Optimize AnimationTree & Improve internals"). In `AnimationMixer::_blend_apply()`, the previous code called `set_position()` / `set_rotation()` / `set_scale()` separately; the optimization merged them into a single `set_transform()` when all three tracks are present: ```cpp // 4.7 problematic code Transform3D transform = Transform3D(Basis(t->rot).scaled(t->scale), t->loc); t_node_3d->set_transform(transform); ``` `Basis::scaled()` operates in **parent/global space (multiplies rows)**, but `Node3D.scale` and the animation `TYPE_SCALE_3D` track are defined as **local space (multiplies columns)**. The correct equivalent is `Basis::scaled_local()`. In 4.6, the separate setters eventually went through `Node3D::_update_local_transform()` → `Basis::set_euler_scale()`, which internally performs `R * S` (diagonal scale matrix then rotation), matching local scale semantics — same as `scaled_local()`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. In Blender, create a node with non-uniform scale (e.g. `(2.5, 1.0, 2.5)`) and rotation. 2. Bake keyframes for position, rotation, and scale (standard glTF TRS animation). 3. Export as GLB and import into a Godot project. 4. Attach a child MeshInstance3D or GPUParticles3D under that node. 5. Play the animation, or simply select the node in the editor and compare the Inspector `Scale` against the original keyframe values — they will differ. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [animation-issue-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29879649/animation-issue-mrp.zip)
